nodes.summary: For every proposition $A$, let $A^*$ be its translation into $\to$ and $\bot$, which keeps atoms and implications and recursively replaces each $B \wedge C$ by $(B \to (C \to \bot)) \to \bot$ and each $B \vee C$ by $(B \to \bot) \to C$. Then $A^*$ is derivable from no hypotheses in classical propositional logic if and only if $A$ is.
nodes.title: The translation into $\to$ and $\bot$ preserves and reflects classical derivability

nodes.summary: Let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be a list of atoms and let $f$ assign a truth value to every valuation of the atoms, such that $f(v) = f(w)$ whenever $v$ and $w$ agree on $x_1, \dots, x_n$. Then for every valuation $v$ that makes $\bot$ false, the Shannon expansion of $f$ over $x_1, \dots, x_n$ has truth value $f(v)$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the Shannon expansion

nodes.summary: For every proposition $A$ and every valuation $v$ that makes $\bot$ false, the translation of $A$ into $\to$ and $\bot$ has the same truth value under $v$ as $A$.
nodes.title: The translation into $\to$ and $\bot$ preserves truth values

nodes.summary: Every Boolean function of the atoms in a finite list is the truth table, on valuations with `⊥` false, of some proposition.
nodes.title: Functional completeness

nodes.summary: Every Boolean function of the atoms in a finite list is the truth table, on valuations with `⊥` false, of a proposition built with `→` alone.
nodes.title: Functional completeness of `→` and `⊥`

nodes.summary: A proposition is built from $\to$ and $\bot$ when it contains no conjunction and no disjunction: every atom (including $\bot$, which is an atom) is, and $A \to B$ is exactly when both $A$ and $B$ are.
nodes.title: Propositions built from $\to$ and $\bot$

nodes.summary: Let $f$ assign a truth value to every valuation of the atoms. The Shannon expansion $S(\ell, f)$ of $f$ over a list $\ell$ of atoms is defined by recursion on $\ell$. For the empty list it is $\bot \to \bot$ if $f$ is true at the valuation that makes every atom false, and $\bot$ otherwise. For the list $x \cdot \ell$ with head $x$ and tail $\ell$,
nodes.title: Shannon expansion

nodes.summary: The translation $A^*$ of a proposition $A$ is defined by recursion on $A$: each atom is unchanged, $(A \to B)^* = A^* \to B^*$, $(A \wedge B)^* = (A^* \to (B^* \to \bot)) \to \bot$ and $(A \vee B)^* = (A^* \to \bot) \to B^*$.
nodes.title: Translation into $\to$ and $\bot$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
